bodies.name: Alpha Centauri A
bodies.identityNote: A is Rigil Kentaurus / G2V, left in Hubble portrait.
bodies.nativeSurface: Hubble optical/near-infrared unresolved binary point sources plus Webb infrared observational graphic. Neither resolves photospheric geography; displayed false colours are not calibrated visible colours.
measured: Kervella2017 H-band interferometric limb-darkened diameter8.502±0.038mas; radius1.2234±0.0053 solar radii using747.17±0.61mas parallax.
The Hubble portrait records A left and B right; released2016-08-29, filters457nm and850nm; exact observing day unverified.
modelled: Adopted representative effective temperature5795K (±19K reference uncertainty) from interferometric radii and bolometric flux, reviewed by Thévenin2023 quoting Morel2018/Kervella2017. Hydrogen/helium plasma and outer convection are stellar-model context, not measured abundance mass fractions.
Thévenin2023 also reports updated radius/temperature alternatives A1.2175Rsun5800K/B0.8591Rsun5236K using Akeson2021 astrometry; catalogue and orbit values preserved.
Webb2025 graphic combines infrared data, subtraction and annotations; source publisher classifies Artwork. S1 remains a candidate, not a confirmed planet or observed stellar surface.
unknown: Resolved convection, actual magnetic spot pattern, calibrated visible intensity/colour, precise abundance fractions and chromospheric geometry.
assumed: Independent two modest dim magnetic patches and finer granulation; all photospheric geography invented, no Sun or another component map reused.
Conceptual observer two photospheric radii from centre, one radius above plasma, artistic120-degree field; no solid ground or physically survivable landing.
Companion lies outside this chosen field; no dated binary orientation, companion angular location or photometric calibration is claimed.
